lines.text: Jo bikes up a hill slowly, then zooms back down. What's her average speed?
lines.caption: Jo bikes up a hill slowly, then zooms back down. What's her average speed?

lines.text: Averaging the two speeds feels right. It's a trap, and there's a second trap hiding in the units!
lines.caption: Averaging the two speeds feels right. It's a trap, and there's a second trap hiding in the units!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's ride this one carefully.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's ride this one carefully.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Jo bikes up a three kilometer hill at twelve kilometers per hour.
lines.caption: Jo bikes up a three kilometer hill at twelve kilometers per hour.

lines.text: She then bikes back down the same hill at ten meters per second.
lines.caption: She then bikes back down the same hill at ten meters per second.

lines.text: What is her average speed for the whole round trip, in kilometers per hour?
lines.caption: What is her average speed for the whole round trip, in kilometers per hour?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? Three kilometers up, then the same three kilometers down.
lines.caption: So what do we know? Three kilometers up, then the same three kilometers down.

lines.text: Watch out: the two speeds use different units. Kilometers per hour, and meters per second.
lines.caption: Watch out: the two speeds use different units. Kilometers per hour, and meters per second.

lines.text: Average speed means total distance divided by total time.
lines.caption: Average speed means total distance divided by total time.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: total distance over total time

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: find the total distance and the total time.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: find the total distance and the total time.

lines.text: First, let's fix the units. Ten meters per second means ten meters every second.
lines.caption: First, let's fix the units. Ten meters per second means ten meters every second.

lines.text: An hour has three thousand six hundred seconds.
lines.caption: An hour has three thousand six hundred seconds.

lines.text: So in an hour she'd go ten times three thousand six hundred, thirty-six thousand meters.
lines.caption: So in an hour she'd go ten times three thousand six hundred, thirty-six thousand meters.

lines.text: That's thirty-six kilometers. So going down, her speed is thirty-six kilometers per hour.
lines.caption: That's thirty-six kilometers. So going down, her speed is thirty-six kilometers per hour.

lines.text: Going up, three kilometers at twelve kilometers per hour takes a quarter of an hour. That's fifteen minutes.
lines.caption: Going up, three kilometers at twelve kilometers per hour takes a quarter of an hour. That's fifteen minutes.

lines.text: Going down, three kilometers at thirty-six kilometers per hour takes a twelfth of an hour.
lines.caption: Going down, three kilometers at thirty-six kilometers per hour takes a twelfth of an hour.

lines.text: That's five minutes.
lines.caption: That's five minutes.

lines.text: In total, she rides six kilometers in twenty minutes.
lines.caption: In total, she rides six kilometers in twenty minutes.

lines.text: Twenty minutes is a third of an hour. So in a whole hour, at that pace, she'd go three times as far.
lines.caption: Twenty minutes is a third of an hour. So in a whole hour, at that pace, she'd go three times as far.

lines.text: Six times three is eighteen. Her average speed is eighteen kilometers per hour.
lines.caption: Six times three is eighteen. Her average speed is eighteen kilometers per hour.

lines.text: The answer is eighteen. That's Choice B!
lines.caption: The answer is eighteen. That's Choice B!

lines.text: Here's a clever shortcut. The length of the hill doesn't change the average, because both times grow together.
lines.caption: Here's a clever shortcut. The length of the hill doesn't change the average, because both times grow together.

lines.text: So pick a friendly length, like thirty-six kilometers!
lines.caption: So pick a friendly length, like thirty-six kilometers!

lines.text: Going up at twelve takes three hours. Going down at thirty-six takes one hour.
lines.caption: Going up at twelve takes three hours. Going down at thirty-six takes one hour.

lines.text: That's seventy-two kilometers in four hours. Seventy-two divided by four is eighteen. Same answer!
lines.caption: That's seventy-two kilometers in four hours. Seventy-two divided by four is eighteen. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the distance makes awkward fractions.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the distance makes awkward fractions.

lines.text: Choose one both speeds divide.
lines.caption: Choose one both speeds divide.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice A, eleven, is the average of twelve and ten. That mixes kilometers per hour with meters per second.
lines.caption: Choice A, eleven, is the average of twelve and ten. That mixes kilometers per hour with meters per second.

lines.text: Choice C, twenty-two, is twelve plus ten. Adding speeds doesn't make sense at all.
lines.caption: Choice C, twenty-two, is twelve plus ten. Adding speeds doesn't make sense at all.

lines.text: Choice E, thirty-six, is just the downhill speed, not the whole trip.
lines.caption: Choice E, thirty-six, is just the downhill speed, not the whole trip.

lines.text: Choice D, twenty-four, is the average of twelve and thirty-six. The units are right, but it's still a trap!
lines.caption: Choice D, twenty-four, is the average of twelve and thirty-six. The units are right, but it's still a trap!

lines.text: She spends fifteen minutes going slowly and only five minutes going fast.
lines.caption: She spends fifteen minutes going slowly and only five minutes going fast.

lines.text: The slow part counts for more time, so the average is lower.
lines.caption: The slow part counts for more time, so the average is lower.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Average speed is total distance over total time. Never just average the speeds.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Average speed is total distance over total time. Never just average the speeds.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Max bikes up a three kilometer hill at nine kilometers per hour.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Max bikes up a three kilometer hill at nine kilometers per hour.

lines.text: He comes back down at five meters per second. What's his average speed, in kilometers per hour?
lines.caption: He comes back down at five meters per second. What's his average speed, in kilometers per hour?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check.
lines.caption: Let's check.

lines.text: Five meters per second is five times three thousand six hundred, eighteen thousand meters an hour.
lines.caption: Five meters per second is five times three thousand six hundred, eighteen thousand meters an hour.

lines.text: That's eighteen kilometers per hour.
lines.caption: That's eighteen kilometers per hour.

lines.text: Going up takes a third of an hour, twenty minutes. Going down takes a sixth of an hour, ten minutes.
lines.caption: Going up takes a third of an hour, twenty minutes. Going down takes a sixth of an hour, ten minutes.

lines.text: In total, he rides six kilometers in thirty minutes.
lines.caption: In total, he rides six kilometers in thirty minutes.

lines.text: Thirty minutes is half an hour, so in a whole hour he'd go twice as far. Six times two is twelve kilometers per hour!
lines.caption: Thirty minutes is half an hour, so in a whole hour he'd go twice as far. Six times two is twelve kilometers per hour!

lines.text: Here's the sneaky part. Averaging nine and eighteen gives more than thirteen.
lines.caption: Here's the sneaky part. Averaging nine and eighteen gives more than thirteen.

lines.text: The real answer is lower, because the slow part takes longer.
lines.caption: The real answer is lower, because the slow part takes longer.

lines.text: If you got twelve, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you got twelve, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: First, make the units match. Then find the total distance and the total time.
lines.caption: First, make the units match. Then find the total distance and the total time.

lines.text: Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Don't average the two speeds!
lines.caption: Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Don't average the two speeds!
